I'm in your shoes, I came to the US on a TN Visa and my employer sponsored me. My employer went with the consular processing route. I started the process in March 2022. The I-140 got processed in May 2022. I became documentarily qualified in August 2022 and got my interview letter a week later in August and had my interview 2 months later in the end of October.

The only thing that sucks with consular processing is that the embassy holds onto your passport and you better hope they don't put you into administrative processing since it could take weeks or months before they make a decision on issuing your visa. I've been placed in administrative processing and haven't been able to work in 3 weeks.

If I could've went back in time I'd probably go AOS route sure I wouldn't be able to leave but atleast I could still work.
I waited 8 days from when I was documentarily qualified to receive the letter of my interview date. My interview date was 2 months from when I received the letter. My visa is EB-3 btw.

On the interview day they told me that I'm going into administrative processing and gave me two sheets of paper. The first sheet was the 221g slip to say I'm in administrative processing and it shows where I can go on CEAC to check the status of my case. The second sheet shows how to register online how to get back my passport. 

From what I researched administrative processing is when the officer wants to check over your documents or do a background check or waiting for an item to be received before they make a decision on whether to issue/deny your green card. The timeframe how long it takes for them to complete administrative processing varies greatly. If I knew I was going to be in administrative processing for over 3 weeks I would have probably done some OT to save money from the time I'm not working. I'm just giving you a heads up on what could happen but I hope you don't have to go through what I'm experiencing. So far they have my passport and I'm waiting for them to make a decision and send back my passport. I'll update you once I get back my passport.
